results.title: HIRING HR Assistant | Avatar New Energy Materials Co.
results.description:
HIRING

HR Assistant | Avatar New Energy Materials Co. Limited

📍 Location: Nasarawa State
Job Type: Full-time
Compensation: ₦130,000–₦160,000 monthly

About the Role

Avatar New Energy Materials Co. Limited, a Chinese company specialising in lithium exploration, mining, and processing in Nigeria, is seeking an entry-level HR Assistant to support recruitment, employee records, staff welfare, and daily HR operations in a mining and industrial environment.

Key Responsibilities

• Assist with recruitment activities, including job postings, CV screening, interview scheduling, and onboarding.
• Maintain and update employee files, records, and HR databases.
• Support employee onboarding and orientation.
• Assist with attendance tracking, leave management, and basic payroll documentation.
• Handle employee inquiries and escalate issues when necessary.
• Support the implementation of HR policies, procedures, and company rules.
• Coordinate training programmes, meetings, and staff activities.
• Assist with employee welfare and disciplinary documentation.
• Maintain the confidentiality of employee information.

• Perform other HR and administrative duties as assigned.

Requirements

• Bachelor’s Degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Public Relations, or a related field.
• 1–2 years of experience is an advantage.
• Basic knowledge of HR practices and Nigerian labour laws.
• Good written and verbal communication skills.
• Strong organisational and record-keeping skills.
• High level of integrity and professionalism.
• Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications.
• Willingness to work in a mining or site environment.
• Open to male and female candidates aged 23–27.

Skills & Competencies

• Attention to detail.
• Time management and multitasking ability.
• Strong interpersonal and communication skills.
• Ability to handle sensitive information confidentially.
• Team-oriented mindset.

How to Apply

📧 Apply via: Send your CV to hr@avtne.com using “HR ASSISTANT” as the email subject.

Application Deadline: 16 November 2026.

results.title: 𝗖𝗕𝗡 𝗠𝗢𝗩𝗘𝗦 𝗧𝗢 𝗘𝗔𝗦𝗘 𝗡𝗜𝗚𝗘𝗥𝗜𝗔–𝗖𝗛𝗜𝗡𝗔 𝗣𝗔𝗬𝗠𝗘𝗡𝗧𝗦 🇳🇬🇨🇳 Nigeria is looking to make financial transactions with China easier as the Central Bank of Nig
results.description:
𝗖𝗕𝗡 𝗠𝗢𝗩𝗘𝗦 𝗧𝗢 𝗘𝗔𝗦𝗘 𝗡𝗜𝗚𝗘𝗥𝗜𝗔–𝗖𝗛𝗜𝗡𝗔 𝗣𝗔𝗬𝗠𝗘𝗡𝗧𝗦 🇳🇬🇨🇳

Nigeria is looking to make financial transactions with China easier as the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) pursues deeper financial cooperation with Chinese institutions.

On October 17, 2026, CBN Governor Olayemi Cardoso disclosed that discussions with the Governor of the People's Bank of China, Pan Gongsheng, had covered cross-border payments, settlement arrangements, financial technology and trade finance.

A planned visit to Beijing is expected to advance these discussions.

But why should Nigerian businesses and investors pay attention?

𝗙𝗜𝗥𝗦𝗧: 𝗜𝗡𝗧𝗘𝗥𝗡𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡𝗔𝗟 𝗣𝗔𝗬𝗠𝗘𝗡𝗧𝗦 𝗠𝗔𝗧𝗧𝗘𝗥.

China is an important source of imported goods, machinery, industrial equipment and other products used by Nigerian businesses.

When cross-border payments are difficult, slow or expensive, businesses can face additional transaction costs and settlement delays.

More efficient payment arrangements could make it easier for Nigerian importers and Chinese exporters to conduct business.

However, the CBN has not yet announced a specific new payment system, implementation date or confirmed reduction in transaction fees.

𝗦𝗘𝗖𝗢𝗡𝗗: 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗡𝗔𝗜𝗥𝗔 𝗔𝗡𝗗 𝗙𝗢𝗥𝗘𝗜𝗚𝗡 𝗘𝗫𝗖𝗛𝗔𝗡𝗚𝗘 𝗠𝗔𝗧𝗧𝗘𝗥.

Businesses involved in international trade need reliable access to foreign currency and efficient settlement channels.

Improved financial cooperation could reduce some operational difficulties, but it does not automatically eliminate foreign-exchange risk or guarantee cheaper imports.

The actual benefits will depend on the payment arrangements eventually agreed upon and how they work in practice.

𝗧𝗛𝗜𝗥𝗗: 𝗖𝗢𝗨𝗟𝗗 𝗧𝗛𝗜𝗦 𝗔𝗧𝗧𝗥𝗔𝗖𝗧 𝗠𝗢𝗥𝗘 𝗜𝗡𝗩𝗘𝗦𝗧𝗠𝗘𝗡𝗧?

The CBN is also interested in stronger financial links with Chinese banks and opportunities to attract investment from Asian markets into Nigerian financial instruments.

Better payment infrastructure and stronger institutional relationships could create additional channels for trade financing and investment.

For Nigeria, the potential benefits include improved access to capital and stronger commercial relationships.

For listed companies, businesses that depend on imported inputs or international trade financing could benefit if the arrangements reduce costs or improve settlement efficiency.

𝗪𝗛𝗔𝗧 𝗦𝗛𝗢𝗨𝗟𝗗 𝗜𝗡𝗩𝗘𝗦𝗧𝗢𝗥𝗦 𝗪𝗔𝗧𝗖𝗛?

Three things:

1. Whether Nigeria and China announce concrete payment or settlement arrangements.
2. Whether the new arrangements reduce transaction costs and delays for businesses.
3. Whether stronger financial cooperation translates into actual investment and improved business activity.

𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗕𝗢𝗧𝗧𝗢𝗠 𝗟𝗜𝗡𝗘:

This is a potentially important development for Nigeria's trade and financial infrastructure, but discussions alone do not guarantee immediate economic benefits.

The real value will become clearer when specific agreements are announced and businesses begin to experience measurable improvements.

Follow for more NGX news and investor-focused explanations of Nigeria's economic developments.

#CBN #NigeriaEconomy #China #NGX

results.title: No exhaustive public list exists of every Tinubu-era foreign investment that has produced confirmed Nigerian jobs.
results.description:
No exhaustive public list exists of every Tinubu-era foreign investment that has produced confirmed Nigerian jobs. Actual FDI inflows remain far below announced pledges.

Examples include the Chinese $250m lithium plant in Nasarawa (Diamond New Energy), which reports over 1,000 direct and 2,000 indirect jobs, and the $200m Zamfara plant (Chinese partners) targeting 2,000 local jobs. The $7bn Ogun DP World seaport deal is still an MoU projecting 50,000 jobs.

results.title: Southeast Nigeria has no direct Atlantic coastline.
results.description: Southeast Nigeria has no direct Atlantic coastline. Proposed sites requiring extensive river dredging: Obeaku (Ukwa East, Abia; feasibility study by China Harbour underway in 2026 via Azumini rivers, ~28 nautical miles). Oseakwa (Ihiala, Anambra, linked to Oguta Imo; claimed deep natural harbor historically). Onitsha is only a limited river port for barges. Viability depends on funding, federal approval and multi-state channels.
